subject: woodlouse
title: Streetlights Trap Thousands of Woodlice in Endless Spinning Circles

scenes.text: Thousands of tiny animals march in a circle, going nowhere.
These are woodlice in Israel. One spinning mill can hold more than 5,000 of them.
Most are females, many carrying eggs, so it isn't a mating ritual.
The trigger is a streetlight. Its beam draws a bright ring on the ground, and they follow the edge.
Once enough pile in, the swirl keeps itself going, and a centipede was seen picking them off.
They're not lost. They're trapped by a ring of light.

description:
On summer nights in Israel, thousands of woodlice walk in circles under streetlights.
A Hebrew University study found white light shining straight down triggers the mills, which can hold more than 5,000 isopods, and a centipede was seen preying on the swirling mass.
Have you ever seen insects acting strangely around a light at night?
first_comment: UV light barely attracted them and strong magnets did nothing at all; only white light pointed at the ground started the spin. Would you switch off your porch light for them?
